title: The robot's state machine
summary: RobotContainer is a state machine too: buttons ask the robot, the robot asks the subsystems.

say.never: Each subsystem is a state machine. The **robot** is one more state machine on top of them, sometimes called a *super state machine*. A robot state like `SHOOT` means "drive normally **and** shoot", so the robot asks the drivetrain for one state and the shooter for another. A kitchen works the same way: the head chef calls "dinner service", and each cook knows what that means for their own station.
say.bit: The robot is a state machine over the subsystems: one robot state asks each subsystem for a state.

board.code:
buttons / autos
         |  robot.setWantedState(SHOOT)
         v
   RobotContainer   (robot states: IDLE, DRIVE, SHOOT)
      |                 |
      v                 v
   drivetrain        shooter
   (ARCADE)          (SHOOT)

say.never: Anything that uses **more than one** subsystem lives in one place: the robot's state machine. Buttons never talk to subsystems; they only ask the robot for a state. That means the same robot state works for a button in teleop **and** for an autonomous routine, so you write it once.
say.bit: Buttons and autos only ask the robot for a state, so each behaviour is written once.

steps.title: In your lesson: the robot's states

say.never: `RobotContainer` already lists the subsystems. Now it also has states: `IDLE` (disabled), `DRIVE` and `SHOOT`. Every loop, before the subsystems run, its `updateLogic` looks at the robot's state and asks each subsystem for the state it needs, with the same `setWantedState` you use everywhere.
say.bit: `RobotContainer.updateLogic` runs first each loop and asks each subsystem for a state.

steps.title: In your lesson: who asks whom

say.never: `Robot.java` asks for `IDLE` when the robot is disabled and `DRIVE` when teleop starts. Your right bumper will ask for `SHOOT` while it is held. Nobody but `RobotContainer` talks to the shooter.
say.bit: Robot.java asks for IDLE or DRIVE; the right bumper asks for SHOOT; only RobotContainer asks the shooter.
